item.title: Inflation hits wallets
item.description: Fijian households and businesses are facing a severe cost-of-living squeeze as headline inflation skyrocketed to 6.1 per cent in June, up from 3.9 per cent in May this year. This increase also marks a significant shift from the -1.2 per cent recorded in the same period last year.
item.content:encoded:
Fijian households and businesses are facing a severe cost-of-living squeeze as headline inflation skyrocketed to 6.1 per cent in June, up from 3.9 per cent in May this year.

This increase also marks a significant shift from the -1.2 per cent recorded in the same period last year.

According to the Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF), this price increase was largely driven by higher fuel and gas prices, alongside higher electricity costs as the impact of Energy Fiji Limited’s (EFL) fuel surcharge took effect.

RBF Governor Ariff Ali said together, those factors directly accounted for approximately 4.5 percentage points of the inflation rate recorded in the month under review.

He said renewed conflict between the United States and Iran led to a sharp increase in global oil prices, with Brent crude oil rising slightly above $US100 per barrel (on July 23) before easing to around $US84 per barrel by July 29.

However, he said prices remained elevated compared with end-June levels.

“As an importer of fuel, Fiji remains vulnerable to such external developments, which could place further upward pressure on domestic fuel prices, transportation costs and broader production expenses,” Mr Ali said in a statement.

“If current oil prices persist, inflation is expected to remain above 6.0 per cent through the end of the year.”

At the same time, foreign reserves remained adequate at around $3.9 billion as of July 30; and sufficient to cover 5.4 months of retained imports.

Mr Ali said foreign reserves were expected to remain at comfortable levels over the medium term, supported in part by planned Government loan drawdowns.

He said while domestic activity continued to be supported by the tourism sector, developments in other sectors indicated some moderation in growth momentum, with softer outcomes recorded in timber, gold doré, cane production and manufacturing.

“On the demand side, consumption activity has shown signs of easing despite support from higher household incomes and strong remittance inflows.

“In contrast, investment activity has remained resilient, supported by higher new investment lending and increased imports of construction-related materials.”

However, Mr Ali said supply side constraints, including higher fuel and freight costs, labour shortages, and election year uncertainty could weigh on investment prospects going forward.

Financial conditions, he said remained accommodative, supported by ample liquidity of $2.0b as of July 29, which had helped keep lending rates low.

He said that had continued to support borrowing by households and businesses and contributed to sustained growth in private sector credit.

He said the strength of the financial system provided an important buffer against temporary domestic and external shocks.

Meanwhile, the central bank board decided to maintain the overnight policy rate at 0.25 per cent following its meeting on July 30.

Mr Ali said slowing economic conditions, coupled with inflation caused by more expensive imports, support the decision to hold the overnight policy rate steady.

item.title: Hotel renews partnership with leadership institution
item.description: Holiday Inn Suva has renewed its strategic partnership with Leadership Fiji, continuing as the official venue partner for their 2026 Executive Leadership Program. This collaboration reaffirms Holiday Inn Suva’s dedication to leadership development in Fiji, providing a professional and centrally located space for the program’s key events while supporting the continued development of leaders across
item.content:encoded:
Holiday Inn Suva has renewed its strategic partnership with Leadership Fiji, continuing as the official venue partner for their 2026 Executive Leadership Program.

This collaboration reaffirms Holiday Inn Suva’s dedication to leadership development in Fiji, providing a professional and centrally located space for the program’s key events while supporting the continued development of leaders across the country.

Holiday Inn Suva general manager Mohammed Feroz said the partnership was more than just providing a venue for the program, but an investment in the people shaping the future of Fiji’s organisations, communities and economy.

He said they were proud to provide an environment where leaders could connect, challenge their thinking and strengthen their ability to lead with purpose.

“As Leadership Fiji celebrates 25 years, Holiday Inn Suva remains committed to supporting the Executive Leadership Program and contributing to a strong, resilient leadership pipeline for Fiji,” Mr Feroz said.

Leadership Fiji chief executive officer Sharyne Fong said Holiday Inn Suva’s ongoing support throughout the years had allowed them to facilitate spaces where leaders could engage and develop.

“As we mark 25 years of Leadership Fiji, we are especially grateful for partnerships such as this, which highlight Holiday Inn Suva’s commitment and belief in our vision to develop and enhance the quality of leaders in Fiji,” Ms Fong said.

The FNPF-owned IHG Fiji Hotels, comprising InterContinental Fiji Golf Resort & Spa, Grand Pacific Hotel Suva and Holiday Inn Suva, have also collectively supported Leadership Fiji’s Executive Leadership Programme since its inception in 2024, as well as its one-day leadership workshop, Leading with Impact.

Leadership Fiji is an independent, non-partisan, non-aligned entity that has been in operation for 25 years, with a network of over 600 alumni, and has a vision to establish a Leadership Centre for Fiji and the Pacific and to expand its programs across all levels of society.

item.title: Call for collaboration to offset high infrastructure costs
item.description: BUILDING telecommunications infrastructure in the Pacific remains an expensive challenge, requiring greater regional collaboration and risk protection to ensure viable services, says Amalgamated Telecom Holdings chief executive officer Ivan Fong. Addressing the Pacific Fiber Conference at the Sheraton Fiji Golf Resort and Spa in Nadi last week, Mr Fong noted the persistent difficulty of making lar
item.content:encoded:
BUILDING telecommunications infrastructure in the Pacific remains an expensive challenge, requiring greater regional collaboration and risk protection to ensure viable services, says Amalgamated Telecom Holdings chief executive officer Ivan Fong.

Addressing the Pacific Fiber Conference at the Sheraton Fiji Golf Resort and Spa in Nadi last week, Mr Fong noted the persistent difficulty of making large-scale investments work in small, low-demand markets.

“Building infrastructure, especially in the Pacific, is an expensive business,” Mr Fong said.

“We don’t always have the demand and customer numbers to make it work on a standalone basis, and for that very reason we need to find how we can collaborate.”

Mr Fong said solutions could range from wholesale agreements and infrastructure sharing to direct partnerships with governments and regulatory authorities to drive market adoption and generate necessary traffic volumes.

He said private investors required downside risk protection without public subsidies crowding out commercial capital.

“We don’t want to have services and capabilities denied just because we can’t close the loop on the investment equation,” he said.

Beyond infrastructure economics, he pointed to the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence as both a promising asset and a growing security concern for regional networks.

item.title: Delta Company wins top cadet drill award
item.description: DELTA Company scooped top honours as the best company in drill during the Natabua High School Cadets annual review in Lautoka last Friday. More than 1100 students marched during the parade, in eight companies and three platoons.
item.content:encoded:
DELTA Company scooped top honours as the best company in drill during the Natabua High School Cadets annual review in Lautoka last Friday.

More than 1100 students marched during the parade, in eight companies and three platoons.

The parade was reviewed by chief guest, Dr Apisalome Movono, the chief executive officer of the Tertiary Scholarships and Loans Service (TSLS).

Award recipients: Baton of Honour – Parade Commander Areeb Ali, Best Company in Drill – Delta Company, Best Male Rifle Platoon in Drill – Charlie 1, Best Female Rifle Platoon in Drill – Delta 1, Best Male Non-Rifle Platoon in Drill – Charlie 2, Best Female Non-Rifle Platoon in Drill – Bravo 3, Outstanding Male Officer – Manasa Vuiwakaya, Outstanding Female Officer – Fane Tuimanono, Outstanding Senior NCO – Aush Singh, Outstanding Junior NCO – Grace Vuiwakaya, Outstanding Cadet – Colour Ensign Ruci Tuitubou, Outstanding Senior Cadet – RSM Solomone Nacagilevu, Outstanding New Cadet – Ratu Tevita Mara, Outstanding Bandsman – Aliyah Elena, Best Organised Classroom – Year 9BHEC3, Best Organised Dormitory – Dorm B.

item.title: BSP Life honours 150-year legacy
item.description: A CELEBRATION of 150 years of service to Fiji brought together Government ministers, senior officials, business leaders, partners and BSP Life staff at the Grand Pacific Hotel in Suva on Monday night. Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka officiated at the milestone event, where guests reflected on BSP Life’s 150-year journey and its contribution to the country’s insurance industry.
item.content:encoded:
A CELEBRATION of 150 years of service to Fiji brought together Government ministers, senior officials, business leaders, partners and BSP Life staff at the Grand Pacific Hotel in Suva on Monday night.

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka officiated at the milestone event, where guests reflected on BSP Life’s 150-year journey and its contribution to the country’s insurance industry.

The celebration also featured the presentation of a $150,000 cheque to the Fiji Wellness Coalition to support national wellness initiatives, alongside a showcase of the company’s history and cultural performances by BSP Life staff.

item.title: Nearly 8,000 marijuana plants seized in Northern Division raid
item.description: Close to 8,000 plants believed to be marijuana have been seized by police during a drug operation at the Bilobiloca farming area in the Northern Division. Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe said the operation was launched following information received from members of the public.
item.content:encoded:
Close to 8,000 plants believed to be marijuana have been seized by police during a drug operation at the Bilobiloca farming area in the Northern Division.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe said the operation was launched following information received from members of the public.

He said police deployed a drone to verify the information, which confirmed the location of the suspected marijuana cultivation site before officers moved in.

ACP Vusonilawe acknowledged the continued support of communities, saying public cooperation had played a vital role in the success of drug raids, resulting in significant seizures and arrests.

“The sharing of information is indicative of community support towards law enforcement efforts, and the Fiji Police Force extends its appreciation for the consistent support towards crime prevention efforts,” he said.

He added that police drug operations go beyond targeting illicit drugs, with officers also focusing on other criminal offences to ensure a comprehensive approach to crime prevention and enforcement.

Police are encouraging members of the public to continue supporting law enforcement efforts by reporting crimes, sharing information or raising concerns about police service delivery through the Crime Stoppers hotline on 1681.

item.title: Public Enterprises portfolio shifted to Kamikamica from Charan Jeath Singh
item.description: Responsibility for Fiji’s public enterprises has been transferred from Minister for Multi-Ethnic Affairs, Culture, Heritage and Arts Charan Jeath Singh to newly sworn-in Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica as part of the latest Cabinet reshuffle. Kamikamica was sworn in yesterday as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises, returni
item.content:encoded:
Responsibility for Fiji’s public enterprises has been transferred from Minister for Multi-Ethnic Affairs, Culture, Heritage and Arts Charan Jeath Singh to newly sworn-in Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica as part of the latest Cabinet reshuffle.

Kamikamica was sworn in yesterday as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Industries, Commerce, Business Development and Public Enterprises, returning to Cabinet after previously serving in the portfolio.

The change means the Ministry of Public Enterprises is no longer under Charan Jeath Singh, who previously held the position of Minister for Public Enterprises, Multi-Ethnic Affairs, Culture, Heritage and Arts.

The Ministry of Public Enterprises is responsible for overseeing and implementing government reform programmes for state-owned enterprises while monitoring their performance and operations to improve efficiency and effectiveness. Its work is guided by the Public Enterprises Act 1996 and the Public Enterprises (Amendment) Act 2002.

The ministry oversees a significant portfolio of government commercial companies, including Fiji Broadcasting Corporation, Airports Fiji Limited, Fiji Public Trustee Corporation Limited, Food Processors (Fiji) Limited, Post Fiji Limited, Fiji Rice Limited, Unit Trust of Fiji Limited, Viti Corp Corporation Limited, Yaqara Pastoral Company Limited and Fiji Hardwood Corporation Limited.

It also has responsibility for several commercial statutory authorities, including the Fiji Electricity Authority, Fiji Meat Industry Board, Housing Authority, Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji, Water Authority of Fiji and the Public Rental Board.

In addition, the ministry oversees government’s majority-owned companies, including Fiji Pine Limited, Pacific Fishing Company Limited, Copra Millers Fiji Limited and Air Terminal Services.

The transfer of the portfolio restores responsibility for public enterprises to Kamikamica, who now assumes oversight of a range of key state-owned entities involved in aviation, utilities, agriculture, transport, housing and other strategic sectors of the economy.

item.title: Yasawa, Mamanuca declared fruit fly emergency areas
item.description: The Yasawa Group and Mamanuca Islands have been declared biosecurity emergency areas following the detection of the Tongan fruit fly ( Bactrocera facialis ), with strict controls now in place to prevent the pest’s spread. A notice published in the Fiji Gazette states that the declaration was made by the Minister for Agriculture and Waterways, Tomasi Tunabuna, under Section 77 of the Biosecurity Ac
item.content:encoded:
The Yasawa Group and Mamanuca Islands have been declared biosecurity emergency areas following the detection of the Tongan fruit fly ( Bactrocera facialis ), with strict controls now in place to prevent the pest’s spread.

A notice published in the Fiji Gazette states that the declaration was made by the Minister for Agriculture and Waterways, Tomasi Tunabuna, under Section 77 of the Biosecurity Act 2008, on the advice of the Biosecurity Authority of Fiji (BAF) and in consultation with the National Disaster Risk Management Council.

The declaration will remain in force for six months from the date of publication in the Gazette.

Under the emergency measures, the movement of a wide range of fruits, vegetables and host materials from the Yasawa Group and Mamanuca Islands is prohibited.

Restricted produce includes mangoes, guavas, papayas, citrus fruits, avocados, breadfruit, starfruit, roses, capsicum, tomatoes, pumpkins, zucchini, cucumbers, melons and other host materials identified by BAF.

The Gazette notice also states that host material includes all fruits found in the Yasawa Group and Mamanuca Islands.

The restrictions are aimed at containing the Tongan fruit fly and preventing it from spreading to other parts of Fiji, where it could pose a significant threat to agriculture and horticultural production.

The notice warns that any person who contravenes directions made under the declaration commits an offence under Sections 79(3) and 94 of the Biosecurity Act 2008 and is liable to the penalties prescribed under Schedule 5 of the Act.

The declaration was made on July 28, 2026, and is signed by Minister for Agriculture and Waterways Tomasi Tunabuna.
